text: First, they consulted Britain's most famous pathologist, Sir Bernard Spilsbury. Could a body convince a Spanish doctor that a man had died at sea? Spilsbury's answer encouraged them. Victims of air crashes over water often died of shock rather than drowning. And in Spain, he advised, detailed post-mortems were rarely carried out unless the cause of death seemed important.
